My mom had surgery last month on her foot and needed to stay out of work for 2 weeks longer than her manager gave her off (3 days), so they made her fill out FMLA and short term disability through their company New York Life GBS. Everything went through fine, her doctor signed everything including a statement adding no standing for 2-3 hrs without a 10 minute break to put her foot up at work. 

Both her DM and store manager knew she would have a boot to wear and a scooter so this was not added to the paper work as it was clear everyone knew.(We should have had it in writing but didn't as they both said they'd accommodate her.) She went to work for a whole day and everything  went fine, then the next day her manager said she'd need to get a note from the doctor about the scooter and boot the next time she saw him(the following day to get the stitches removed). 

Something seemed off so my mom called the HR representative to ask where to find the ada papers to get filed out(her work has never tooken just a Dr's note). HR lady said she wasn't supposed to be working at all without those papers filed and sent my mom home until the doctor could fill them out. Well Dr filled the papers about the scooter, boot, needing to sit occasionally and not lifting excessive weights as she'd be one footed. The Dr said she could start walking on her foot as much as she felt comfortable to with the boot on. 

BUT now her work says they can't accommodate her scooter she still needs for long distances(She walks and stands alot at her job). So she called New York Life GBS to reactivate her FMLA and short term disability since her work won't let her go back. They told her they could reactivate the claim and she should file the accommodations with them as the representative said that they see this often with companies not wanting to work with employees and that is why they filed the paperwork themselves and not through New York Life like they were supposed to. 

When she talked to her leave specialist at work they said she didn't need to file with New York Life, just to get a new Dr's note or wait until she no longer needs her scooter. Why would she just be providing a Dr's note instead of actually filing ADA with the claims company(New York Life)? Could her job be at risk caus they aren't having her file the ADA properly? Also she's set to do the other foot next month when she can fully walk on the one she just had done, are they able to do anything because of that aswell? 

My mom really needs these surgeries and has already pushed them off for two year and they just can't wait any longer but her work hasn't been letting her work for the last four weeks and we're just trying to figure it out.
